scenario.question: We move to combat and declare ALL EIGHT of our creatures as attackers against seat-2 (jarad-graveyard, 17 life), whose only untapped creature is Reclamation Sage (2/1); seat-3's Abaddon is tapped and seat-4 is not being attacked. We then activate Goblin Burrows once. (a) Resolve every attack trigger in Comprehensive Rules order and state the total power attacking seat-2 and the non-combat damage dealt to it. (b) Is seat-2 dead before our end step, taking the single most favourable block Reclamation Sage can make? Cite a rule for each trigger, for tokens that enter tapped and attacking, and for seat-4's Blind Obedience if it changes any of it.
notes: SUPERSEDED — this scenario was lifted by a bridge that silently omitted permanents, and both resolutions here reasoned from an incomplete board. Three defects, all found by the rules-checker reading THIS artifact and all fixed 2026-09-28: a creature with a characteristic-defining power (`Creature * / *`) never reached the board; an Aura was discarded as an instant; and a token was registered only when it ACTED, so the lift listed 10% of live tokens. Re-lifted as 010-sim-g61-t27-precombat-main. Kept because its resolver/checker exchange is what found the bugs — read it as history, never as a line.

HAND UNKNOWN BY CONSTRUCTION. A Forge log is an event stream, not a snapshot, so the bridge writes {'unknown': 6}. The question is therefore scoped to the battlefield: a line that assumed a card in hand would be a proof about a board this game never had.

WHY THIS BOARD. It is the widest our seat reached in 100 seeded games at standard-v3 (7 other bodies beside the commander, 2.0% of commander-out turns). It is also a board we were LOSING from: 5 life, blocking on three of the next four turns, and Zada was recast on turn 31 because she died. Both facts are the point of lifting it.

THE ACTIONS ARE AUTHORED, NOT OBSERVED. Forge's AI did not attack here — it blocked on three of the next four turns and Zada died before turn 31. `observed_in_log: false` on both, because the whole point of the lift is to ask what a pilot would have done with the board the AI was handed.

steps.action: Set the frame. Turn 27, precombat main, we hold priority at 5 life; seat-2 (jarad-graveyard) 17, seat-3 (abaddon) 36, seat-4 (sythis-enchantress) 41. We move to combat. Anything that kills seat-2 must land in the combat damage step, which precedes the postcombat main phase and the ending phase that contains our end step. BOARD PROVENANCE: this board was lifted from a run of the zada-v1 BRANCH list, and Hanweir Garrison — the engine of this line — is NOT in goblin-storm's sleeved 99 (scenario-facts card_membership.NOT_IN_THE_DECK). Every figure below is reachable on the branch list and NOT on the deck's current 99.
steps.effect: The kill window is the combat damage step of turn 27, before our end step. The line is branch-only.

citations.quote: A turn consists of five phases, in this order: beginning, precombat main, combat, postcombat main, and ending.

steps.action: Declare attackers. We choose all eight of our creatures: Hanweir Garrison (2/3 Human Soldier), Zada, Hedron Grinder (3/3 Goblin Ally), General Kreat, the Boltbringer (2/2 Goblin Soldier), and five Human Tokens. All eight are listed untapped on the board. Because this is a multiplayer game in which we may attack any opponent, we announce a defending player for each: all eight attack seat-2. Seat-3's Abaddon is tapped and seat-4 is not attacked. TWO PREMISES THE LIFT CANNOT CONFIRM: (i) summoning sickness is not reconstructed by the bridge (extras.reconstruction_notes), so the declaration assumes each of the eight has been under our control since the turn began; (ii) the five Human Tokens carry pt: null in the lift — scenario-facts therefore files them under other_permanents rather than creature_bodies, and we read them as 1/1 red Human creature tokens because Hanweir Garrison, whose text mints exactly that token, is the only Human-token source on the board. That disagreement with scenario-facts is stated, not resolved by us.
steps.effect: Eight attackers against seat-2. Declared power 2 + 3 + 2 + (5 x 1) = 12.

citations.quote: The chosen creatures must be untapped
continuously since their most recent turn began
the active player announces which player, planeswalker, or battle each of the chosen creatures is attacking
a player can also choose to attack only one player during a particular combat

steps.action: Attack triggers trigger, at the moment of declaration. Hanweir Garrison: 'Whenever this creature attacks, create two 1/1 red Human creature tokens that are tapped and attacking' — it is among the declared attackers, so this triggers once. General Kreat's first ability: 'Whenever one or more Goblins you control attack, create a 1/1 red Goblin creature token that's tapped and attacking' — Zada (Goblin Ally) and General Kreat (Goblin Soldier) are both declared attackers; Hanweir Garrison is a Human Soldier and the Human Tokens are Humans, so the Goblin count that arms this is two. The condition reads 'one or more', and one declaration of attackers is one trigger event, so it triggers ONCE, not once per Goblin. Both abilities are ours; we put them on the stack in the order we choose before we get priority. WE CHOOSE: General Kreat's first trigger on the BOTTOM, Hanweir Garrison's on TOP, so Garrison's resolves first. The order changes no total below — only the interleave shown in steps 4 to 6, which is what the question's 'Comprehensive Rules order' asks to see.
steps.effect: Two triggered abilities on the stack: Hanweir Garrison's (two Human tokens) and General Kreat's first (one Goblin token).

citations.quote: Abilities that trigger on a creature attacking trigger only at the point the creature is declared as an attacker.
An ability triggers only once each time its trigger event occurs.
Any abilities that triggered on attackers being declared or that triggered during the process described in rules 508.1 are put onto the stack before the active player gets priority
in APNAP order, puts each triggered ability they control

steps.action: Resolve the TOP trigger, Hanweir Garrison's: it creates two 1/1 red Human creature tokens that are tapped and attacking. Neither creating effect names a defending player, so we choose one for each token as it enters: seat-2. The clause quoted below governs EVERY token this line mints, the Goblin token of step 6 included. Each is 'attacking' but never 'attacked', so neither Hanweir Garrison's trigger nor General Kreat's first trigger fires again off them — there is no loop here. GENERAL KREAT'S FIRST TRIGGER IS STILL ON THE STACK, unresolved, and it stays there: the two Human tokens entering causes General Kreat's SECOND ability to trigger twice, and a triggered ability is put on the stack the next time a player would receive priority and becomes the TOPMOST object — i.e. on top of Kreat's first trigger, which is why the drains resolve before the Goblin token exists.
steps.effect: Two 1/1 red Human tokens enter the battlefield tapped and attacking seat-2. Attacking power 12 -> 14 across 10 attackers. Kreat's first trigger remains on the stack beneath two new entry triggers. FLOOR, NOT A TOTAL: the lift annotates every Human Token 'observed acting in the log; tokens that only sat are not listed', and extras.tokens_unobserved_resolutions records you: 4 — four token-creating resolutions our seat had that the lift did not place on the board (two of them confirmed from the log as Krenko's Command making two 1/1 red Goblin tokens at global turn 23). Every power and attacker figure from here on is therefore a floor.

citations.quote: If a creature is put onto the battlefield attacking, its controller chooses which defending player, planeswalker a defending player controls, or battle a defending player protects it’s attacking as it enters the battlefield (unless the effect that put it onto the battlefield specifies what it’s attacking). Similarly, if an effect states that a creature is attacking, its controller chooses which defending player, planeswalker a defending player controls, or battle a defending player protects it’s attacking (unless the effect has already specified). Such creatures are “attacking” but, for the purposes of trigger events and effects, they never
the next time a player would receive priority. See rule 117, “Timing and Priority.” The ability becomes the topmost object on the stack.

steps.action: Seat-4's Blind Obedience, checked once for all three tokens this line mints — the two Humans of step 4 and the Goblin of step 6. Its oracle text is 'Extort ... Artifacts and creatures your opponents control enter tapped.' We are its controller's opponent, so the clause is a continuous effect that replaces how our tokens enter, and it applies to all three. But each token is already created 'tapped and attacking' by the ability that made it, so applying Blind Obedience produces an identical result — the token enters tapped either way. Blind Obedience says nothing about attacking, and it is rule 508.4 (quoted in step 4) that makes these creatures attacking, so the attacking status is untouched. Its extort half triggers only when ITS controller casts a spell; seat-4 casts nothing in this line.
steps.effect: Blind Obedience changes NOTHING about this line: the tokens were already entering tapped, and they remain attacking. Zero damage, zero power, zero life difference.

citations.quote: Some replacement effects modify how a permanent enters the battlefield.
A keyword ability that lets you gain life and have opponents lose life whenever you cast a spell.

steps.action: THE CR ORDER, shown rather than flattened. General Kreat's second ability reads 'Whenever another creature you control enters, General Kreat deals 1 damage to each opponent.' (i) The two Human tokens that entered in step 4 each triggered it. Both of those triggers went on the stack above General Kreat's still-unresolved FIRST trigger, so they resolve first: 1 damage to each opponent, twice. seat-2 17 -> 15, seat-3 36 -> 34, seat-4 41 -> 39. (ii) NOW General Kreat's first trigger resolves, creating one 1/1 red Goblin creature token tapped and attacking; the effect names no defending player, so we choose seat-2 as it enters. (iii) That entry is a third 'another creature you control enters' event — the Goblin token minted by General Kreat's own first ability is still 'another creature' — so the second ability triggers a third time and resolves: seat-2 15 -> 14, seat-3 34 -> 33, seat-4 39 -> 38. Three separate events, three triggers. Each resolves for 1 damage to EACH opponent, and damage dealt to a player by a source without infect is life loss. Had we stacked the two attack triggers the other way, the Goblin token would enter first and its drain resolve first; the totals are identical.
steps.effect: PER-OPPONENT: 3 non-combat damage, so 3 life lost by each of seat-2, seat-3 and seat-4. POD TOTAL: 9. These two figures are not interchangeable. Seat-2 17 -> 14; seat-3 36 -> 33; seat-4 41 -> 38. All three tokens are now on the battlefield: attacking power 15 across 11 attackers, both figures FLOORS (step 4). Nobody is at 0, so no state-based action fires yet.

citations.quote: If a creature is put onto the battlefield attacking, its controller chooses which defending player
An ability triggers only once each time its trigger event occurs.
Damage dealt to a player by a source without infect causes that player to lose that much life.

steps.action: HOLD the Goblin Burrows activation until after blockers are declared. The scenario's action list puts the activation second, and the order inside combat is load-bearing: if we pump in the declare attackers step, seat-2 simply blocks the pumped creature and the +2/+0 is absorbed. We therefore pass priority in the declare attackers step and act in the declare blockers step, where the active player gets priority after blockers are declared.
steps.effect: We reach the declare blockers step with 11 attackers, 15 power, Goblin Burrows untapped, and five untapped lands besides it.

citations.quote: Second, the active player gets priority.

steps.action: Seat-2 declares blockers, taking its single most favourable block. Seat-2 is the only defending player attacked, and Reclamation Sage (2/1 Elf Shaman) is its only untapped creature — its other permanents are Ripples of Undeath and three tapped lands. The Sage may block exactly one attacking creature. None of our 11 attackers has an evasion ability, so every attacker is a legal choice. ENUMERATING the choices by the power the block takes off the player: Zada 3; Hanweir Garrison 2; General Kreat 2; each of the eight 1/1 tokens 1; and declining to block, 0. The maximum is 3, so the best block available to seat-2 is Reclamation Sage on Zada. A blocked creature assigns its combat damage to its blockers, not to the player.
steps.effect: Reclamation Sage blocks Zada. Zada's 3 power is removed from the damage going to seat-2. Unblocked power: 15 - 3 = 12 across 10 attackers.

citations.quote: The defending player chooses which creatures they control, if any, will block.
the defending player chooses one creature for it to block
A restriction may be created by an evasion ability (a static ability an attacking creature has that restricts what can block it).
A blocked creature assigns its combat damage to the creatures blocking it.

steps.action: Now activate Goblin Burrows: '{1}{R}, {T}: Target Goblin creature gets +2/+0 until end of turn.' The ability goes on the stack and its costs are paid on announcement: {R} from a Mountain, {1} from a second Mountain, and Goblin Burrows itself taps as part of the cost — which is why it is available exactly ONCE this turn. THE LAND ACCOUNTING: we control six lands, all six untapped at the cut; this activation taps three of them — Goblin Burrows plus two of our three Mountains — leaving exactly three untapped: ONE Mountain, Reliquary Tower and Fountainport, which is what final_state.you.lands_still_untapped records. A second {1}{R} pump is therefore unaffordable in coloured mana even before Goblin Burrows' own tap is counted. The target must be a Goblin creature, so the legal set is Zada, General Kreat and the new 1/1 Goblin token; Hanweir Garrison and all seven Human tokens are Humans and cannot be targeted. Zada is blocked, so we target an UNBLOCKED Goblin: General Kreat (2/2 -> 4/2) or the Goblin token (1/1 -> 3/1). Either adds the same 2 power to what reaches seat-2.
steps.effect: Unblocked power to seat-2: 12 + 2 = 14. Had we instead activated before blockers, seat-2's best block takes the pumped creature and only 12 power reaches it — the timing is worth exactly 2 power, which is the whole margin.

citations.quote: The player announces that they are activating the ability.
The remainder of the process for activating an ability is identical to the process for casting a spell

steps.action: Combat damage step. Each attacking and blocking creature assigns damage equal to its power; the ten unblocked attackers assign to the player they are attacking, seat-2. Assignments, enumerated over all ten unblocked attackers: Hanweir Garrison 2, five original Human tokens 5, two new Human tokens 2 — that is 9 — plus the two unblocked Goblins. If General Kreat is the Goblin Burrows target: Kreat 4 and the Goblin token 1, so 9 + 5 = 14. If the Goblin token is the target: token 3 and Kreat 2, so 9 + 5 = 14. Either choice assigns 14. Zada is blocked and assigns its 3 to Reclamation Sage; the Sage assigns its 2 to Zada. All of it is dealt simultaneously and no player may act in between.
steps.effect: 14 combat damage to seat-2, which is 14 life lost. Seat-2: 14 -> 0. Reclamation Sage has 3 damage marked on it against toughness 1, and Zada 2 damage against toughness 3; what that does to each of them is a state-based action, checked in step 12.

citations.quote: Each attacking creature and each blocking creature assigns combat damage equal to its power.
An unblocked creature assigns its combat damage to the player, planeswalker, or battle
A blocked creature assigns its combat damage to the creatures blocking it.
No player has the chance to cast spells or activate abilities between the time combat damage is assigned
Damage dealt to a player by a source without infect causes that player to lose that much life.

steps.action: Boggart Shenanigans is checked and contributes NOTHING. Its text is 'Whenever another Goblin you control is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, you may have this enchantment deal 1 damage to target player or planeswalker.' The only permanent that dies in this combat is Reclamation Sage, which is an Elf Shaman controlled by seat-2 — it is neither a Goblin nor ours, so the trigger event never matches. No Goblin of ours dies: Zada takes 2 as a 3/3, and no other attacker is blocked. Any total that credited Boggart Shenanigans a point of reach here would be wrong.
steps.effect: Boggart Shenanigans deals 0 damage in this line. The 3 non-combat damage in step 6 is the whole of the non-combat total.

citations.quote: that ability automatically triggers

steps.action: State-based actions, and WHEN they are checked — which is the half of (b) the previous pass asserted. Combat damage was dealt as a turn-based action of the combat damage step (step 10); the next thing that step does is give the active player priority. Whenever a player WOULD get priority, the game first checks every state-based-action condition and performs all applicable ones simultaneously as a single event, so the check happens inside the combat damage step, before anyone actually receives priority. Two conditions are met at that check: seat-2 has 0 life, so seat-2 loses the game; and Reclamation Sage has 3 damage marked on it with toughness 1, so it has been dealt lethal damage and is destroyed. The combat damage step sits in the combat phase, which is two phases before the ending phase that holds our end step — so the answer to (b) is yes, and the moment is cited rather than assumed. WHAT THIS IS NOT: we are at 5 life and seat-3 is at 33 with seat-4 at 38 after step 6. Removing seat-2 is an ELIMINATION, not a win. WHAT COULD STILL BREAK IT: seat-2's hand is five cards the lift does not name (hand unknown by construction) and its mana.open is 0 with all three of its lands tapped, so only a card with an alternative cost requiring no mana could interfere. We do not assume such a card and we do not assume its absence.
steps.effect: Seat-2 loses the game at the state-based-action check that precedes the combat damage step's priority pass on turn 27 — two phases before our end step. Reclamation Sage is destroyed in the same single event. Exactly lethal ON THE BOARD AS LIFTED: 3 non-combat + 14 combat = 17 against 17 life, margin ZERO. Because the best block available to seat-2 removes at most 3 power (step 8's enumeration), seat-2 dies under every legal block, and under no block it takes 3 + 17 = 20. And because 15 power / 11 attackers are FLOORS (step 4), any of the four unobserved token resolutions that left a body on the battlefield only adds unblocked power: the floor is already lethal, so the line is more robust than the margin-zero figure reads, not less.

citations.quote: If a player has 0 or less life, that player loses the game.
the game checks for any of the listed conditions for state-based actions, then performs all applicable state-based actions simultaneously as a single event
Third, the active player gets priority.
the total damage marked on it is greater than or equal to its toughness, that creature has been dealt lethal damage and is destroyed
A turn consists of five phases, in this order: beginning, precombat main, combat, postcombat main, and ending.

final_state.summary: ALL EIGHT ATTACK, THEN PUMP AFTER BLOCKS: 15 power attacking seat-2 after triggers, 3 non-combat damage to it, and seat-2 is DEAD in the combat damage step of turn 27 with a margin of exactly ZERO. (a) Declared power 12 (Hanweir Garrison 2, Zada 3, General Kreat 2, five 1/1 Human tokens 5). Two attack triggers fire once each: Hanweir Garrison makes two 1/1 Human tokens, General Kreat's Goblin-attack trigger makes one 1/1 Goblin token (once, not once per Goblin). TOTAL POWER ATTACKING SEAT-2 = 15 across 11 attackers, 17 if Goblin Burrows' +2/+0 is counted on an attacker — and BOTH FIGURES ARE FLOORS, not the board: the lift lists only tokens observed acting and extras.tokens_unobserved_resolutions records you: 4 unobserved token-creating resolutions for our seat (two confirmed from the log as Krenko's Command making two 1/1 red Goblin tokens at global turn 23). Any body those left adds unblocked power, so the floor being lethal makes the line MORE robust. NON-COMBAT DAMAGE TO SEAT-2 = 3, from General Kreat's second ability triggering three times off the three tokens entering: 3 PER OPPONENT, 9 ACROSS THE POD. Boggart Shenanigans adds 0 (no Goblin of ours dies; Reclamation Sage is a seat-2 Elf). Seat-4's Blind Obedience changes nothing — the tokens already enter tapped and it does not touch 'attacking'. (b) YES. Reclamation Sage's best block is Zada, the largest attacker, removing 3 power; unblocked power 12, plus 2 from Goblin Burrows targeting an unblocked Goblin, is 14 combat damage against 17 - 3 = 14 life. Seat-2 hits 0 and loses to a state-based action, checked at the moment the active player would get priority in the combat damage step (704.3 + 510.3), two phases before our end step (500.1); Reclamation Sage is destroyed by 704.5g in the same check. THE TRIGGERS RESOLVE IN CR ORDER: Hanweir Garrison's trigger, two Humans, their two drain triggers on top of Kreat's unresolved first trigger (17 -> 15), then Kreat's first trigger, the Goblin token, and the third drain (15 -> 14). The block enumeration puts the maximum power any single block can absorb at 3, so seat-2 dies under every legal block. THE TIMING IS THE WHOLE MARGIN: Goblin Burrows must be activated in the DECLARE BLOCKERS step, after blocks. Activated first, as the scenario's action order reads, seat-2 blocks the pumped creature and only 12 reaches it — seat-2 survives at 2. TWO THINGS THIS IS NOT. It is not a line the sleeved deck can run: Hanweir Garrison is NOT in goblin-storm's 99 and both triggers of this engine start with it, so the whole board and total belong to the zada-v1 BRANCH. And it is not a win: we are at 5 life, seat-3 is at 33 and seat-4 at 38 after the drain, so this is an ELIMINATION of one seat.

totals.floors_note: 15 power and 11 attackers are FLOORS. The lift lists only tokens observed acting (annotation on every Human Token) and extras.tokens_unobserved_resolutions records you: 4. Two of the four are confirmed from the log: Krenko's Command created two 1/1 red Goblin tokens at global turn 23. Unobserved bodies can only raise unblocked power, cannot add an attack trigger (General Kreat's first ability triggers once per declaration however many Goblins attack), and cannot raise the power any single block absorbs above 3 (Zada remains the largest attacker), so the margin-zero kill stands and widens.
totals.lethal_margin_note: margin 0 on the board AS LIFTED; a lower bound, since the attacking figures are floors

notes: HANWEIR GARRISON IS NOT IN THE SLEEVED 99. scenario-facts card_membership.NOT_IN_THE_DECK names it; it is present in data/decks/goblin-storm/branches/zada-v1/cards.json and absent from data/decks/goblin-storm/cards.json. Hanweir Garrison supplies two of the three tokens, hence two of the three General Kreat drain triggers and 9 of the 15 attacking power (its own 2 plus seven 1/1 Human tokens). This resolution is a proof about the zada-v1 BRANCH list, not about the deck's current 99.

DISAGREEMENT WITH scenario-facts, STATED NOT RESOLVED: your_board.creature_bodies lists three bodies and files the five Human Tokens under other_permanents, because the lift records pt: null for them. The question treats all eight as bodies. We read the tokens as 1/1 red Human creature tokens on the grounds that Hanweir Garrison — the only Human-token source on the board — mints exactly that, and we flag that the lift itself does not state their power.

SUMMONING SICKNESS IS NOT RECONSTRUCTED (extras.reconstruction_notes). The declaration in step 2 assumes all eight have been under our control since the turn began; if any had not, rule 302.6 would remove it from the attack and its power from the total.

THE ACTIONS ARE AUTHORED, NOT OBSERVED (observed_in_log: false on both). Forge's AI did not attack from this board; it blocked on three of the next four turns and Zada died before turn 31. This is what a pilot could have done, proven by citation — not what happened.

ORDER OF OPERATIONS IS THE FINDING. The scenario lists the attack then the Goblin Burrows activation, and read literally that order costs the kill: pump before blocks and seat-2 blocks the pumped creature for 12 damage and survives at 2. Pump in the declare blockers step and it is exactly 14, exactly lethal.

THE 15 AND THE 11 ARE FLOORS, NOT TOTALS. FLOOR, NOT A TOTAL: the lift annotates every Human Token 'observed acting in the log; tokens that only sat are not listed', and extras.tokens_unobserved_resolutions records you: 4 — four token-creating resolutions our seat had that the lift did not place on the board (two of them confirmed from the log as Krenko's Command making two 1/1 red Goblin tokens at global turn 23). The direction is one-way favourable: an unobserved body adds unblocked power, adds no attack trigger (Kreat's first ability triggers once per declaration), and cannot raise the maximum power a single Reclamation Sage block absorbs above 3, because Zada at 3 is still the largest attacker. So the exactly-lethal 14 against 14 is a LOWER BOUND on the damage and the kill is more robust than the margin-zero figure reads. Declared power 12 is likewise the power of the eight bodies the lift lists.

open_questions.question: Is there a version of this board reachable on the SLEEVED 99 — i.e. a 17-life kill with General Kreat and Boggart Shenanigans but no Hanweir Garrison — and what does it need?

Its four findings — the uncited death timing, the missing 704.5g, the step-9 land miscount and the flattened CR order — are fixed in this block, which is re-checked below.
